title: RCT to Compare Stress-CMR Using Mobile MRI vs. MRI for Inpatients
official: Comparison of the Use of an Outpatient/Mobile MRI Procedure With an Inpatient MRI Procedure in Adult Patients With Known or Suspected Coronary Heart Disease in a Randomized Open-label Study
summary:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the clinically relevant manifestation of atherosclerosis affecting the coronary arteries. CAD is associated with an increased risk of morbidity and mortality and typically presents as angina pectoris or dyspnea. Non-invasive imaging techniques are recommended for the diagnosis of CAD. Of particular importance is stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), which is distinguished from other recommended diagnostic modalities by its high diagnostic accuracy and the absence of exposure of patients and healthcare professionals to ionizing radiation. Consequently, stress perfusion CMR has been assigned a Class I recommendation in international cardiology guidelines.

The aim of this study is to demonstrate the feasibility of transferring the clinical routine workflow for the diagnostic evaluation of patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) from stationary, specialized centers to mobile MRI units.

This will be demonstrated by comparing two groups. In one group, stress CMR examinations will be performed using mobile MRI units, while in the other group, examinations will be conducted in stationary imaging facilities. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups.

interventions.name: Cardiac stress CMR examinations for clinical diagnostic in adult patients with suspected coronary artery disease

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Adults based one of the following criteria:

* Male or female subjects aged ≥18 years
* Clinical indication for invasive cardiac diagnostic evaluation in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD)
* Patient fully responsible and can understand/sign the study from a legal aspect
* Patients who have provided written informed consent to participate in the study and to the processing of their personal data

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patient refusal to participate
* Any contraindication to perform an Stress-Perfusion MRI exam
* Contraindication to the cardiac MRI examination (e.g. inability to hold breath; severe claustrophobia, metallic devices such as pace makers)
* Sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus
* Known pregnancy or lactation
